questions.q: What problem does Delta Sharing solve that GRANT (Lesson 42) doesn't?
options: Sharing a table with a completely separate organization outside your own metastore, who may not have a Databricks account at all
Sharing a table with a user inside your own workspace
GRANT and Delta Sharing solve exactly the same problem
Delta Sharing only works for row-level security, not table access
questions.explain: GRANT assumes the recipient is a known principal inside your metastore; Delta Sharing assumes they're not.

questions.q: What are the three objects Delta Sharing introduces?
options: Shares (bundles of tables), Providers (the sharing organization), and Recipients (the receiving organization)
Catalogs, Schemas, and Tables
Grants, Revokes, and Masks
Volumes, Metastores, and Workspaces
questions.explain: This mirrors GRANT's shape — privilege, object, principal — but the principal is an entire outside organization.

questions.q: Why doesn't a Delta Sharing recipient need a Databricks account to read a shared table?
options: Delta Sharing works across the open Delta Lake protocol itself, readable by any compatible client like plain Python, Pandas, or Power BI
Recipients are automatically given a free Databricks account
Shared tables are converted to CSV files before sharing
Delta Sharing requires the recipient to use Azure specifically
questions.explain: This is Delta Sharing's real distinguishing feature — not a Databricks-to-Databricks-only connection.

questions.q: Does adding a table to a share bypass column masks or row filters from Lesson 43?
options: No — a shared table can still carry masks or row filters, applied to the recipient the same way they'd apply to an internal user
Yes, sharing a table removes all governance from it entirely
Only row filters are bypassed; column masks still apply
Only column masks are bypassed; row filters still apply
questions.explain: Delta Sharing extends who governance reaches — it doesn't turn governance off.

options: The external organization receiving the shared access
A new internal user account within the metastore
A new catalog created specifically for sharing
A backup copy of the share's tables
questions.explain: GRANT SELECT ON SHARE ... TO RECIPIENT then gives that external organization access to the share's tables.
